name: settings-accordion-affordance
note: UAT batch 4. RED-FIRST vs main: (a) sections were flush rows split by a hairline - the grammar of a LIST, so nothing said they open; they are grouped cards with real gaps now; (b) the expand handle was a filled U+25BE triangle (a desktop <select> glyph) - it is a stroke chevron drawn from borders now, the mobile disclosure standard; (c) .setLbl sat at 600/~1rem against an .accBtn at 800/1.08rem, a step too small to read as hierarchy ('settings text too similar to sections') - it takes the app's caption convention (small uppercase micro-caps) so it cannot be mistaken for a heading; (d) the Theme description is gone. The hierarchy assert compares the two MEASURED sizes rather than pinning either number, so a later type-scale change cannot make it pass while the hierarchy is flat again.

steps.label: layout settle gate: await document.fonts.ready before any geometry or type assert
every section is an individually distinct card - its own surface AND border AND radius, not a hairline-separated row
and real space between them - the gap is what says 'separate openable thing' (they were flush before)
the expand handle is a drawn stroke chevron, not a font glyph: empty content with real border strokes, so the weight is ours at every DPI
the header row clears a comfortable mobile tap row (>=52px, was 44)
the chevron flips on open - measured as an actual transform change, not merely an aria attribute

UAT: an inner setting label is unmistakably subordinate to its section heading - strictly smaller, dimmer, and micro-capped. Compares the two measured values so a future type-scale change cannot pass this while flattening the hierarchy again
UAT: the Theme description is gone (the segmented control names its own three options - the sentence restated them)
removing that sentence did not collapse the space above the next label - the old rule keyed the gap on a PRECEDING hint, so deleting the hint silently closed it
no horizontal overflow at 412 with the new card insets
